title: A Quarter-Past Seven
treatment: Cold-open bedroom threshold at a quarter-past seven. Watson wakes to Holmes fully dressed by the bed; a frightened young lady waits below. One embodied choice: how to enter the case.
runtime_goal: Ground the player in Watson's body and habit, establish the improper hour and pressing client, and land a posture-setting first choice within a few turns.
player_desire: Understand what is wrong and decide how to meet it.
live_pressure: An agitated client waits below at daybreak; first impressions will be formed with or without you.
opening_image: Thin morning light on the mantel clock reading a quarter-past seven; Holmes, already fully dressed, stands over your bed with that quiet alertness which means some singular business is afoot.
player_affordances: Rise at once with human sympathy
Dress with professional composure to hear facts first
Pause Holmes for one precise question about the visitor before descending
Ask Holmes about the hour or the client
Observe the thin morning light and mantel clock
canon_must_keep: It is a quarter-past seven, an hour Holmes is seldom astir
A young lady in considerable excitement insists on seeing Holmes in the sitting-room below
Watson is Holmes's intimate friend and habitual companion who follows cases from the outset
allowed_variance: Watson's exact tone of surprise/resentment
Which posture the player chooses and how it is voiced
Whether Watson asks a clarifying question
forbidden_expansions: Do not reveal Helen's name, Stoke Moran, Julia, Roylott, the whistle, or the bruises
No supernatural framing
No modern colloquial speech
source_extracts: "Very sorry to knock you up, Watson," said he, "but it's the common lot this morning."
"No; a client. It seems that a young lady has arrived in a considerable state of excitement, who insists upon seeing me."
"My dear fellow, I would not miss it for anything."
exit_condition: The central pressure resolves when Watson has committed to (or pointedly deferred) joining Holmes downstairs, his entering posture established, so the scene can hand off to the sitting-room.
next_bridge: With his posture chosen, Watson descends the stair beside Holmes toward the sitting-room where the veiled visitor waits.

title: It Is Fear, It Is Terror
treatment: The sitting-room. A lady in black rises from the window; her shivering is fear, not cold. Holmes demonstrates the return-ticket and mud deduction, and invites her to lay the case before them.
runtime_goal: Deliver first proof of the detective promise through observed deduction and earn Helen's trust in proportion to the chosen posture.
player_desire: Take the measure of this frightened woman and see whether Holmes's method is real.
live_pressure: A terrified stranger is on the edge of breaking; how she is received shapes how freely she will speak.
opening_image: A lady in black, heavily veiled, rises from the window-seat; her gloved hands tremble in the firelight though the morning is not cold.
player_affordances: Reassure Helen or hold professional reserve
Notice details of her appearance (grey-shot hair, hunted eyes)
React with admiration to Holmes's deduction
Prompt Holmes or Helen to begin
Offer coffee or the fire
canon_must_keep: "It is fear, Mr. Holmes. It is terror."
Holmes deduces the dog-cart drive and morning train from the return ticket and seven mud-splashes
Holmes takes genuine interest and pledges the same care he gave Mrs. Farintosh
allowed_variance: Depth of Watson's reassurance based on M01 posture
Order of the deduction beats
Whether the case-book/Farintosh detail is surfaced or left as optional lore
forbidden_expansions: Do not yet give Julia's death account or the family history
No mystical framing of the deduction; keep it clue-anchored
No romance subplotting
source_extracts: "It is not cold which makes me shiver," said the woman in a low voice
"The left arm of your jacket is spattered with mud in no less than seven places... There is no vehicle save a dog-cart which throws up mud in that way"
"before whom you can speak as freely as before myself"
exit_condition: Resolves when Helen is settled and reassured enough to begin her account, her trust calibrated to how the player received her.
next_bridge: Steadied enough to speak, Helen draws a breath and begins the history of Stoke Moran and the man who rules it.

title: The Roylotts of Stoke Moran
treatment: Helen's account of Stoke Moran and Roylott, delivered as choosable probes: the ruined Saxon family, the Calcutta doctor who beat his butler to death, the violent temper, the cheetah and baboon, the isolated joyless household. Ends on the mention of Julia's death.
runtime_goal: Convert front-loaded family history into interactive testimony where the player's questions (intuition vs procedure) shape which motive and menace threads are drawn out.
player_desire: Learn who Roylott is and why this household is dangerous.
live_pressure: The backstory is long and could smother momentum; the player must mine what matters before dread cools.
opening_image: Helen sits forward in the firelight, her prematurely grey hair and worn face testifying to years of strain as she speaks of an ancient family reduced to one mortgaged house.
player_affordances: Probe Roylott's past (Calcutta, the butler, the prison term)
Ask about the will and the sisters' finances
Ask about the animals and the gipsies
Follow procedure with pointed factual questions or follow intuition toward the ominous
Note Helen's prematurely grey hair as evidence of the household's strain
canon_must_keep: Roylott is the last of an ancient Saxon family reduced to a mortgaged Stoke Moran house
He trained in Calcutta, beat his native butler to death, and served prison time
He keeps a free-roaming cheetah and baboon and consorts with wandering gipsies
The mother's bequest passes to Roylott while the daughters reside, with sums on marriage
allowed_variance: How much history the player draws out vs leaves as optional lore
Order of probes
Whether financial detail is deep or deferred to M07
forbidden_expansions: Do not narrate Julia's death scene here (that is M04)

Keep exposition to what the player elicits; do not dump the whole ledger unprompted
source_extracts: "the Roylotts of Stoke Moran, on the western border of Surrey"
"he beat his native butler to death and narrowly escaped a capital sentence"
"he has at this moment a cheetah and a baboon, which wander freely over his grounds"
exit_condition: Resolves when the player has drawn out enough of Roylott's character and the household's peril, and Helen turns toward the subject of her sister's death.
next_bridge: Her voice lowering, Helen comes at last to the night her sister died, and the account darkens into the fatal room.

title: The Speckled Band
treatment: Julia's last night, breathed at full length: the whistle at three a.m., the smell of cigars, the locked doors, the wild stormy night, the scream, the low whistle and metallic clang, Julia swaying into the corridor and dying with 'the speckled band.' Then Holmes's inquest probing establishes the sealed room and his 'deep waters' dissatisfaction.
runtime_goal: Let the session's core dread land unhurried, then hand the player active forensic inquiry into the locked-room facts.
player_desire: Grasp exactly how Julia died and why the room seems impenetrable.
live_pressure: The account is harrowing and the facts refuse an ordinary explanation; the puzzle tightens as each escape route is sealed.
opening_image: Helen relives the wild stormy night: a low clear whistle in the silence, a metallic clang, and her sister swaying into the corridor to gasp of a speckled band before she died.
player_affordances: Press Helen for precise details of the whistle and clang
Ask whether she could swear to what she heard
Probe the coroner's findings on door, shutters, walls, floor, chimney, and poison
Ask what 'the speckled band' might mean
React to Holmes's dissatisfaction
canon_must_keep: Julia dies gasping "It was the band! The speckled band!" pointing toward the Doctor's room
A low whistle and a metallic clang were heard on the fatal night
The room was sealed: fastened door, barred shutters, solid walls and floor, staple-barred chimney; no poison found
Holmes calls these "very deep waters" and is not satisfied by the gipsy explanation
allowed_variance: How much inquest detail the player elicits
Order of questioning
Whether the charred match/match-box detail is surfaced now or noted lightly
forbidden_expansions: Do not reveal the snake, ventilator theory, or clamped bed yet
No graphic gore; render death through Julia's convulsions, pallor, and cry
No supernatural resolution of the whistle
source_extracts: "Oh, my God! Helen! It was the band! The speckled band!"
"the door had been fastened upon the inner side, and the windows were blocked by old-fashioned shutters with broad iron bars"
"These are very deep waters," said he; "pray go on with your narrative."
exit_condition: Resolves when the death account and the sealed-room facts are fully surfaced and the locked-room impossibility is felt as an open question.
next_bridge: As the impossibility settles, Helen confesses she now sleeps in that very room, and the danger turns from history to the present hour.

title: The Bruised Wrist
treatment: Testimony's close. Helen reveals she now sleeps in the death chamber and heard the whistle last night. Helen leaves re-veiled; Holmes and Watson agree the case demands a same-day trip, ending on the door bursting open.

player_desire: Protect Helen and settle whether to act now or gather more first.
live_pressure: Helen is already back in the fatal bed and heard the herald of death last night; the danger is immediate and personal.
opening_image: Holmes gently draws back the frill of black lace at Helen's wrist to reveal five little livid spots, the marks of four fingers and a thumb printed on the white skin.
player_affordances: React to the bruise reveal with anger, gentleness, or restraint

Confirm the plan to visit Stoke Moran that day

forbidden_expansions: Do not resolve the full theory (that is the vigil setup)

Do not let Watson out-deduce Holmes
source_extracts: "I suddenly heard in the silence of the night the low whistle which had been the herald of her own death."

"It is precisely for that reason that we are going to Stoke Moran this day... But what in the name of the devil!"
exit_condition: Resolves when Helen has departed reassured, the same-day trip is committed, and the door bursts open to interrupt the pair.
next_bridge: The door is dashed suddenly open, and an enormous man fills the frame, transferring the danger from testimony to the room itself.

title: The Bent Poker
treatment: Midpoint intensification. Roylott fills the doorway, demands what Helen has said, and is met by Holmes's bland civility about crocuses and draughts. He insults, threatens, and bends the steel poker before storming out; Holmes calmly straightens it again.

player_desire: Stand your ground without provoking catastrophe, and take Roylott's measure.
live_pressure: An enormous, uncontrollable man is threatening bodily harm in the room, having traced Helen.
opening_image: A huge man in top-hat and frock-coat fills the doorway, hunting-crop swinging, his great yellow bird-of-prey face turning from one of you to the other.
player_affordances: Support Holmes's cool deflection or move to physically interpose
Answer Roylott with defiance or hold silence
Observe his dress, bird-of-prey features, and the bent poker
Show concern that Helen was traced
React to Holmes straightening the poker
canon_must_keep: Roylott is enormous, dressed in top-hat, frock-coat, gaiters, carrying a hunting-crop, with bird-of-prey features
Holmes answers provocation with bland understatement (weather, crocuses, draught) and does not become heated

Holmes straightens the poker afterward

forbidden_expansions: Holmes must not rant or match aggression

source_extracts: "It is a little cold for the time of the year," said Holmes.
"I am a dangerous man to fall foul of! See here." ... he seized the poker, and bent it into a curve
"When you go out close the door, for there is a decided draught."
exit_condition: Resolves when Roylott has stormed out, the threat has been weathered without escalation, and Holmes has answered with the straightened poker.
next_bridge: With Roylott gone and the poker straightened, Holmes sets out to learn the man's true motive, returning near one o'clock with the figures in hand.

title: An Excellent Argument
treatment: Holmes returns near one o'clock with the will worked out: the income falls, each daughter's marriage would cripple Roylott, proving the strongest motive. He arms Watson with the Eley's No. 2 and calls the cab for Waterloo.
runtime_goal: Deliver motive clarity (evidence vs speed) and arm the player, converting suspicion into a case with a why and a weapon.
player_desire: Understand what Roylott stands to lose and be ready for danger.
live_pressure: Roylott now knows they are interested; there is no time for dawdling.

next_bridge: The shutters proving impassable, Holmes leads you within, to the middle bedroom where Julia died and where Helen now sleeps.

title: The Dummy Bell-Rope
treatment: The death chamber interior. Low ceiling, gaping fireplace, worm-eaten oak panelling, the clamped narrow bed, the Wilton carpet. Holmes crawls the floor and walls, then tugs the thick bell-rope by the pillow: a dummy, not attached to any wire, fastened to a hook just above a ventilator that opens into the next room, not outdoors.

player_desire: Find what is wrong with this innocent-looking room.
live_pressure: The clues are subtle and the answer is nearly in reach; missing them leaves Helen in the fatal bed tonight.

title: The Signal in the Dark
treatment: Final cash-out. On the lawn Holmes gravely warns Helen her life depends on compliance and lays out the signal plan: feign a headache, when Roylott retires open the shutters and set the lamp as a signal, then withdraw to the old room. From the Crown Inn they watch Roylott drive past and a light spring up. In gathering darkness Holmes assembles the clues — ventilator inferred from the cigar smell, the clamped bed, the dummy rope — and Watson commits to the dangerous vigil.

next_bridge: Hold one brief beat of earned clarity as the middle window burns steady across the black lawn, then present Choice S1_C4 in period voice; the session closes on Watson's chosen commitment posture with the lit window as the carry-forward summons into the dreadful vigil of Session 2.
